        it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in
        the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is
        reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.

        Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>",
        rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings
        list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic,
        when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to
        read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that
        story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in
        `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be
        read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

        is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, each story's Send, the
        ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled,
        their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal
        from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still
        be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted
        or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.

        The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the
        theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review",
        names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its
        findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and
        "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at
        once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside
        its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is
        paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends;
        nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second
        research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.

        The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research
        it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still
        shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the
        application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed
        or approved.

Planning can now research a topic read-only, and afterwards pauses until you explicitly resume or approve. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 86 files.

- **Research** (`.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#research`): started from a "Research" button on the Backlog heading, or from a story's menu.
  - It runs read-only: it can read the project and the web and change nothing.
  - A new built-in `research.pi` prompt asks for findings, not changes: what it found and where, linked to files and lines, what it's unsure of, and suggestions. It may end with proposals.
  - Progress shows in the same panel as drafting.
- **Findings:** saved as markdown in `.suspense/planning/research/`.
  - They're listed under the Backlog, and under the story that asked for them.
  - Each opens in its own body tab and can be deleted.
- **Paused** (`#paused`): once research ends, planning pauses.
  - Sending is disabled while paused: Send sprint, each story's Send, the ribbon's Send Sprint and the shortcut. Proposals are never added by themselves.
  - Editing the plan and accepting or rejecting proposals one at a time still works.
- **Seeing the pause:**
  - A warning-coloured "Paused for review" bar names the research and links to its findings.
  - The bar has "Resume" and "Approve and send sprint" buttons. Only those end the pause.
  - The Planning tab shows a pause icon, and the ribbon's Planning tab a dot.
- **Persistence:** the pause is saved in `order.json`, so it survives closing the project, restarting and reloading.

content.text:
Stories can no longer be sent on their own: every new story lands in Next sprint, and sending the sprint is the only way a story reaches work. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 86 files.

- **No per-story Send:** the hover Send button on story rows is gone. The spec now says plainly that nothing in Planning, the palette or the ribbon sends a single story.
- **Sending one story:** make it the only story in Next sprint and press Send sprint. Failed or cancelled stories go out again the same way.
- **Everything is added to Next sprint:** new stories, duplicates, accepted "New story" proposals and Ask cards all go to the end of Next sprint. From there you can move a story to the Backlog to wait.
- **Ask cards:** the Ask card button is now "Add to sprint".
- **The ribbon:** its New Story button adds to Next sprint too.
- **Keyboard:** Ctrl+Enter no longer sends a story. It now moves the focused story between Next sprint and the Backlog. That choice is mine.
- **While paused:** the pause now only has to block sending the sprint.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `Planning` `#stories`, `#creating`, `#sprint`, `#proposals`, `#paused` and `#keyboard`, `RibbonPlanningTab` `#commands`, and `AskConversation` `#suggested-prompts`.

input.new_string:
Sending the sprint moves its stories into a "Current sprint" section,
        above Next sprint, shown only while it holds a story, so Next sprint
        is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the
        sprint after. A story in Current sprint keeps its place, its row
        showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking
        it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited
        there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, the section
        offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into a
        muted, collapsed "Done" list beneath the Backlog, and those that
        failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in
        their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint
        is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.

    autoStart:
        Next sprint can start on its own: a "Start automatically" switch on
        Next sprint's heading, beside Send sprint, its tooltip saying the
        next sprint starts as soon as the current one is done. It starts
        off, and is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, so it is kept
        across reloads and restarts.

        While it is on, once every story of Current sprint has ended Done,
        the current sprint closes by itself, as Close sprint closes it, and
        Next sprint, if it holds a story, is sent at once, as Send sprint
        sends it, with nobody having to start it; and while no sprint is
        current, a story added to an empty Next sprint starts it the same
        way. A sprint that ended with a story failed, cancelled, or stopped
        never starts the next by itself: it waits, Close sprint offered as
        ever, and the switch's row says, in the theme's warning colour, why
        the next didn't start. Nor does the next start while planning is
        paused, as the paused section says: it starts once the pause is
        ended by Resume, or Approve, if the switch is still on. An empty Next
        sprint starts nothing.

        Each time a sprint starts by itself, a passive notification says
        so, "Next sprint started: 4 stories", with a link that opens
        Planning, and the debug log records it. Turning the switch off
        never stops a sprint already sent; it only keeps the next from
        starting by itself.

Next sprint can now start on its own. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 86 files.

- **New "Current sprint" section** (`#sprint`): sending a sprint now moves its stories into a "Current sprint" section above Next sprint, so Next sprint empties and fills up for the following sprint. I added this so "the next sprint" has a clear meaning.
  - Stories in Current sprint can't be moved or edited.
  - Send sprint is disabled while a sprint is current.
  - Close sprint moves the Done stories to the Done list, and the failed, cancelled or stopped ones back to the start of Next sprint.
- **"Start automatically" switch** (`.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#auto-start`): it sits on Next sprint's heading, is off by default, and is saved with the plan.
  - **When it fires:** when every story in Current sprint ends Done, the sprint closes and Next sprint is sent with no one pressing anything. With no sprint running, adding a story to an empty Next sprint starts it the same way.
  - **When it doesn't:** if a story failed, was cancelled or stopped, or while planning is paused after research. The switch's row says why. Once the pause is lifted, it carries on if the switch is still on. An empty Next sprint starts nothing.
  - **Notice:** each automatic start shows a passive "Next sprint started: N stories" notification and is written to the debug log.
  - **Turning it off:** this never stops a sprint that's already running.

    specGrounding:
        A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written
        from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the
        spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it
        changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component,
        or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as
        every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton
        slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the
        @{ModeSystemPrompts} says, and the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts} tells it to.

        Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story`
        block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the
        compiled reference heading it comes from, as
        `.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#sprint`, with a short line
        of what in it the story touches, and the story's prompt names those
        elements and links to them, as a prompt written for a mode does, so
        the run it is sent to reads them first. Only elements the drafter
        found are cited: a link must point at a heading that exists in the
        compiled reference, and the application checks each one when the
        proposal arrives, dropping any that doesn't, with a muted note on
        the card saying which link it dropped and why.

        Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for
        something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead
        of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match",
        with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec
        has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no
        element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card
        says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with
        "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.

        The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt,
        as a short list, each element's name and section as a link that
        opens the compiled reference there, a "No match" entry muted with a
        small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted,
        listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in
        its row's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or
        added to by hand from the compiled reference.

content.content:
## Layout

Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24 pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.

## States

Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is missing.
- Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
- Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
- Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
- Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, or Paused, and a story not yet sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".

## Drafting

Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than the Backlog's heading.

## Proposals

The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, able to read the project and change nothing, and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says; a block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so.

## Spec Grounding

A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) tells it to.
Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story` block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the compiled reference heading it comes from, as `.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#sprint`, with a short line of what in it the story touches, and the story's prompt names those elements and links to them, as a prompt written for a mode does, so the run it is sent to reads them first. Only elements the drafter found are cited: a link must point at a heading that exists in the compiled reference, and the application checks each one when the proposal arrives, dropping any that doesn't, with a muted note on the card saying which link it dropped and why.
Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match", with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.
The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt, as a short list, each element's name and section as a link that opens the compiled reference there, a "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in its row's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or added to by hand from the compiled reference.
Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at its top, "New story" in the theme's accent or "Add to" and the story's title in Spec's or the story's own mode's colour; its title, its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.
Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into Next sprint, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Next sprint" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens it.
Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

## Research

The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.
Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

## Paused

Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, the ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled, their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.
The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review", names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends; nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.
The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed or approved.

## Keyboard
## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.

Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.

        Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a
        single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and
        sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in
        small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at
        its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels
        beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels
        apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in
        fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up
        down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the
        title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of
        their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24
        pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and
        every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.

content.content:
states:
        Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way
        wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is
        missing.

        \\
        - Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration

content.text:
This is the same request as an earlier polish pass, so this time I tightened the parts that have been added to Planning since then. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 86 files.

- **Order on the page** (`#layout`): pause bar, then Current sprint, Next sprint, Backlog, Findings, and Done, collapsed. Each is headed on the same rhythm.
- **Three shared parts** (`#parts`):
  - **Rows** (36px, fixed columns): stories, steps, findings and Done.
  - **Panels**: an open story, drafting and research, each with a 32px heading and a right-aligned footer, primary action last.
  - **Cards**: proposals and finding summaries.
  - **Labels:** every button reads what it does, never an icon alone.
  - **Pause bar:** a fixed 40px row.
- **States worded for each part** (`#states`): each part now gets its own wording for empty, loading, paused and error.
  - **Story list:** empty messages per section, skeleton rows while loading, and a read or save error that names the file.
  - **Research:** a live progress line, "No findings yet.", an "Incomplete" marker on stopped findings, and Try again that keeps your question.
  - **Pause:** the warning bar, with the Send buttons disabled and saying why.
  - **Proposals:** "No stories proposed." with Draft again, plus the warning for proposals with no spec cited.
- **Keyboard** (`#keyboard`):
  - Ctrl+Shift+D opens Draft stories and Ctrl+Shift+R opens Research.
  - F6 jumps between the pause bar, sections and an open panel.
  - Tab reaches Resume and Approve, a story's steps, Add step and citations, and the Start automatically switch, which toggles with Space.
  - Focus never lands on hidden or disabled controls. After an action it stays put or moves to what the action created.
- **Fix:** the proposal-card text had ended up under Spec grounding after an earlier edit. It now has its own section, `#proposal-cards`.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `Planning` `#layout`, `#parts`, `#states`, `#drafting`, `#proposals`, `#proposal-cards`, `#research`, `#paused`, `#auto-start` and `#keyboard`.

Write the spec so it describes the application as it should be once the prompt is met, and constrains the code. Once you finish, the spec will be built and the same prompt sent to a coding agent, with your reply, to change the code to match it; so end your reply by saying what you changed in the spec and which anchors the code should follow.

When the work is about Suspense, its modes, its prompts, or its questions, or you are to write a prompt or a question for the user, first read .suspense/suspense-fluency.md once in this conversation, unless you already have: it is how Suspense works.

Open a .pi file only to change it. Once you have changed the spec, run `piton check` and fix every error it reports, then run `piton build` and check the result in the refreshed reference under .claude/reference, not by reading the source again. Never finish with a spec that `piton check` or `piton build` reports errors in.

Once you have read what the change depends on, and before your first change, write the constraints this task must meet to .suspense/history/1791805571-AskProposesTasksAsNewStoriesOrAdditions3.understanding.md, once. It is a Markdown list and nothing else: one line per constraint, at most twelve, each a single short, specific statement of what must be true, written as a link to the compiled reference file it comes from, such as `- [The chain tab has no bottom border in combined mode](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chain)`. Only list what the spec says; leave out anything you are deciding yourself. Replace a constraint when you learn it was wrong rather than adding another.

End with a reply of a few sentences saying what changed, or for a question, the answer, not a recap of the work or of what you read.

**Already in place:**
- **Research:** a read-only run whose findings are saved and can be read (`#research`).

**What I added** (`.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#paused`): "nothing is implemented" now also covers a sprint that's already underway.
- **Held:** current-sprint stories still waiting in the queue are held in place, marked "Held for review", with their lane waiting. A story's next step is held the same way.
- **Not held:** a story already running when the pause began finishes, since stopping it would leave work half done. The bar says how many are still running.
- **After the pause:** once you resume or approve, everything held carries on in its original order.

The spec already said this from your earlier request, so I only closed one loophole. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 86 files.

**Already in place:**
- **Where stories go:** every story is added to the end of Next sprint, whether from New story, Ctrl+N, a duplicate, an accepted proposal or an Ask card.
- **No sending a single story:** stories have no Send of their own, and sending the sprint is the only way they reach work.

**What I added** (`.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md#sprint`): a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat input or the queue to be sent from there. Its menu has no "Send" or "Edit in chat input". Prompts written in the chat input aren't stories and still send as before, but once something is a story, the sprint is its only route to work.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `Planning` `#sprint`, `#stories` and `#creating`, `RibbonPlanningTab` `#commands`, and `AskConversation` `#suggested-prompts`.
